summary.control_interpretation: Same-function, behavior-preserving compilation control, not a pure address-alignment experiment. The normal guard and conversion remain unchanged; normal conversion counts and registers match in the recorded row/small-tile ISA. Exceptional branch code has fewer static instructions. Native finite/operator checks pass. Regular/tall timed prefill tile assembly is not part of this control ISA archive; no prefill improvement or occupancy claim follows from it.

workload.phase_scope: Each phase resets history; decode is not continuation after prefill. One warmup of each phase precedes r1.
workload.context: mx context512; llmx model logical context262144 with lazy backing. Actual pp/tg token streams match; allocated KV layouts differ.

limitations: Two calls per workload/arm in forward/reverse order; no statistical certainty from two samples.
All four arms run in the same Linux container/image and physical MI50 with four CPU threads. Historical rates remain separate.
mx allocates max(512,p,n) context; llmx retains model logical context with lazy 64-token Vulkan backing. Token streams/reach match, allocated KV layouts do not.
Model loading and warmups lie outside reported rates but inside process activity windows. Unknown activity stays unknown.
Numerical/HF/split/server qualification and unchanged-type controls are separate retained work, not proved by these speed calls.
Control interpretation requires the parent-reviewed emitted-code/ISA proof; merely naming an arm control is not a measured layout band.
Short-lived processes between samples may be missed; disappeared/new and inaccessible processes are retained as coverage limits. Unavailable GPU counters are not zero.
The control changes fallback instruction order in the same F16 helper. Seven F16 ISA modules change; normal guard/conversion counts remain the same. It is not a pure address-layout perturbation.
The control ISA archive covers the row and small tile; it does not establish identical timed tall-tile instruction structure or occupancy.
All 16 calls retained. Two samples per arm/workload; r1 SD0 is not repeatability evidence.
Whole-call activity and rusage include loading, warmup and both phases. No phase-specific activity attribution.
Boundary samples can overlap calls. Arm totals are descriptive and cannot be summed into unique observations.
Missing/new/departed process observations remain unknown. GPU ranges have no process attribution.
Original eight-call screen remains separate; no pooled statistic, gate waiver or universal parity claim.
